slides.title: How an LLM turns your words into its next word
slides.summary: Follow “I went to bank to deposit” through every stage of an LLM, until it predicts the next word.
body: This chapter puts the whole Transformer architecture chapter together on one example. The model is given “I went to bank to deposit” and has to predict what comes next.
<mark>Every stage turns the same 6 tokens into new numbers. Only the last token's numbers are used to pick the next word.</mark>

body.note: To keep every number readable, this is a toy model: each token gets 4 numbers, with made-up names (money, place, action, grammar). GPT-2 uses 768 numbers, and none of them have names. The token IDs are GPT-2's real ones.

figure.alt: One sentence through every stage of a tiny LLM. Text: “I went to bank to deposit”. Tokens: I, went, to, bank, to, deposit. GPT-2 token IDs: 40, 1816, 284, 3331, 284, 14667; both “to” tokens share 284. Each ID picks a row of numbers, its embedding, and a small position vector is added, giving 6 rows of 4 numbers. In the transformer block, attention lets each word look back: “deposit” gives “bank” 34% of its attention, while “bank” can't look ahead at “deposit”. After attention and the feed-forward layer are added, “deposit”'s money slot grows from 0.80 to 0.96 to 2.65. Then a final norm, a score per word and softmax: money 65%, cash 26%, some 4%, my 3%, the 2%, river 0.3%. The model picks “money”, appends it and runs again.
figure.caption: The whole journey on one page. The next slide lets you step through it.

slides.title: Step through it yourself
slides.summary: Click through all 12 stages. Every number is computed live by a tiny model in your browser.
body: Press Next step, or click any stage's name. On Attention and Feed-forward, pick a token to see its own row.
<mark>Watch the last token, “deposit”: its numbers are the ones that decide the next word.</mark>

ul: Blue cells are positive numbers, red are negative; stronger colour means bigger.
In the attention grid, each row is a token looking back. Dots mark later tokens it can't see.

body.more: How close is this to a real model?
body.text: The steps are the same as GPT-2's, in the same order. The differences are size and training: GPT-2 has 768 numbers per token, 12 heads, 12 layers and weights learned from huge amounts of text. This toy has 4 numbers, 1 head, 1 layer and hand-picked weights, so the numbers can be followed by eye.

slides.title: From text to numbers
slides.summary: Tokens, then IDs, then a row of numbers per token, plus a position vector.

ul: Tokens: the tokenizer splits the text into 6 tokens.
IDs: each token becomes its number in GPT-2's vocabulary.
Embeddings: each ID picks its row from the embedding table.
+ Position: a small vector for each slot is added.

body: <mark>Both “to” tokens get ID 284 and the same embedding. Adding position is what tells them apart.</mark>
The result is the input: 6 rows (tokens) × 4 numbers. GPT-2's input for this sentence would be 6 × 768.

body.text: The tokenizer and its vocabulary are covered in Tokens; the embedding table and position vectors in Token + position.

viz.html: Numbers are (money, place, action, grammar). Values are illustrative; IDs are GPT-2's.

slides.title: Inside the block: “deposit” meets “bank”
slides.summary: Attention lets “deposit” look back at “bank”; feed-forward then boosts its money meaning.
body: Each token looks back at the tokens before it. “deposit” spends most of its attention on itself and on “bank”.
<mark>“bank” can't see “deposit”, because it comes later. It's “deposit” that looks back at “bank”, so by the end of the sentence the money meaning wins.</mark>
Attention's output is added to “deposit”'s vector. Then the feed-forward layer, working on “deposit” alone, sees money and action together and pushes the money slot up. That's added too.

body.note: A real model repeats this block many times (12 in GPT-2), so meanings are refined step by step.

body.text: Words get their meaning from context. Attention is how one token pulls in information from the others.

viz.html: Where “deposit” looks. Its attention adds up to 100%.

slides.title: The prediction: “money”
slides.summary: The last token's vector is scored against every word, and softmax turns the scores into probabilities.

ul: Final norm: “deposit”'s vector is rescaled one last time.
Scores: it's compared with every word in the vocabulary. Words that point the same way score high.
Softmax: the scores become probabilities that add up to 100%.

body: <mark>“money” wins with 65%. “river” gets 0.3%: the context made the money meaning of “bank” win.</mark>
The model appends “money” and runs again on the longer text. A full stop is a likely next pick, and then the end token.

body.more: Does it always pick the top word?
body.text: No. Apps usually sample, so “cash” would sometimes win. Temperature and top-p control how adventurous the choice is.
Generation is a loop: predict one token, append it, run again.

viz.html: Next-token probabilities after “I went to bank to deposit”. Values are illustrative.
